review.title: Check the players
review.intro: Tracking is unsure about these players: say who is outlined in yellow. The questions that matter most come first.
review.matchIntro: The whole match, to correct its actions. Click the bar to go to a moment: it shows each rally, each touch and, in red, each report. Correct the touches on the right, then “Validate rally”; nothing changes on the page before “Apply”.
review.oddMark: Not the same person as the other pictures
review.oddHint: A picture shows someone else? Click it, then say who it is if you know.
review.moreHint: These pictures look like {{name}}. Click those showing someone else, then confirm: the others will be {{name}}.
review.moreNone: No more pictures look like them.

step.training: Training the who-touched model on your answers (a few minutes)…

review.error: The answer was not saved: is the review server still running?
review.mergeQuestion: Are no. {{a}} and no. {{b}} the same person?
review.video: Video of the moment to check
review.pieceNote: Player numbers are the tracking's, not the jerseys'.
review.mergeNote: These two players are never on court at the same time: perhaps one person.
review.cutWhere: That moment is outside the outlined piece: click while the yellow frame shows.
review.cutDone: Cut at {{at}}: the two pieces become two players once applied.
review.cutNote: Does the outlined person change? Click “The person changes here” (or C) at that moment: the two parts will be two players.
review.conflictNote: Your answers link them: a piece most likely shows both. Cut where the person changes, or forget the wrong answer, then apply.
review.conflictApply: Apply your answers to part them.
review.conflictMarks: Pictures marked as someone else, given to one of them:
review.claimMarks: Pictures marked in a card, and who you said they were:
review.diagnose: Two people in the pictures? Cut (✂) between the last picture of one and the first of the other. Only one? Forget the answer that doesn't match the picture.
review.claimSplit: Your answers give this piece ({{from}} – {{to}}) to several people: cut (✂) between them.
review.moments: Your other answers in this piece (click to see the moment):
review.pinned: All your answers giving a piece to {{names}}
review.pinnedNote: They may sit under the wrong name. If the picture doesn't show the person named, pick who it is.
review.mergeWarn: Careful: this answer would join {{names}}, who carry different names, into one player. Save it anyway?
review.doneApply: Apply your answers to update the match page.
review.doneNothing: Tracking has no doubt left that matters.
review.namesIntro: Give each player a name; the same name on two numbers makes them one. The jersey number is optional. Apply to update the page. Keyboard: ↑ ↓ move between players, ← → between pictures, Space marks the picture (type the name, Enter), N names the player.
review.name: Name
review.sameName: Same name as {{players}}: they will become one player. For two different people, add the initial of the surname.
review.applyBoth: Apply the answers and the names
review.touchQuestion: Who touches the ball in the yellow frame?
review.touchNote: Only the slow-motion part counts. If nobody touches the ball, answer "Nobody".
review.aceQuestion: Who misses the reception of this serve?
review.aceNote: Pick who in the receiving team should have taken the serve; if it lands out of everyone's reach, answer "Nobody".
review.reportNoTouches: No touch found in this rally.
review.reportCommentHelp: A note for you, never put online.
review.reportWrongCallHelp: The referee gave the point to the wrong team. Pick as winner the team that got the point, then tick this.
review.reportRedoHelp: The point is to be replayed: the score stays.
review.reportStartHelp: A rally starts here. Then add its serve and touches.

review.nobody: Nobody touches it in the frame

review.backupFailed: The backup on the server failed at {{at}}: next try in 10 minutes.
review.hostedFailed: The online page could not be updated at {{at}}: try again later.
review.reportRallyPlay: Replay this rally from its start
review.progressLeft: About {{left}} left · done around {{end}} · running for {{elapsed}}

review.rerunConfirm: Learn from your answers? The match analysis runs again: a few minutes to 40 minutes, the review waits. Your answers are kept.
review.hostedBehind: The online page lacks your latest changes.
review.progressIntro: What your answers taught the analysis, measured at each "Learn from my answers".

about.touches: Every time the player touches the ball, whatever the action.
about.serves: The serves, which put the ball in play.
about.aces: The serves that win the point outright: they land in the other court with nobody touching them.
about.serveFaults: The serves into the net or out.
about.receptions: The first touches on the other team's serve, aces conceded included.
about.missed: The receptions lost. An ace conceded counts against the player nearest to where it landed.
about.unattacked: The receptions after which the team sends the ball back or loses it without attacking.
about.rated: The receptions' mean rating, out of 5, from where the next touch is played: 5 within 1.5 m of the setter's target (1 m off the net, between zones 2 and 3), 3.3 within 3 m, 1.7 further or sent straight over the net, 0 for a fault.
about.sets: The team's second touches, the ones that set up the attack.
about.attacks: The third touches, hit above the head to send the ball to the other team.
about.kills: The attacks that win the point outright: they land in the other court with nobody touching them. A dig or block of the other team that loses the ball counts as its fault.
about.attackFaults: The attacks out, into the net, landing on the player's own side or blocked for a point.
about.defended: The attacks the other team touches and keeps in play, with a dig or a block.
about.relances: The third touches sent back without attacking, with a forearm or an overhead pass.
about.relanceFaults: The free balls out, into the net or landing on the player's own side.
about.blocks: The balls touched at the net right after the other team's attack.
about.blockPoints: The blocks that land in the other court.
about.blockFaults: The blocks that go out or land on the player's own side.
about.blockDefended: The blocks after which the rally goes on.
about.digs: The first touches on the other team's attack or free ball.
about.digFaults: The digs lost: the ball lands, goes out or into the net.
about.unattackedDigs: The digs after which the team sends the ball back or loses it without attacking.
about.points: Balls played that land in the other court.
about.faults: Balls out, into the net or landing on the player's own side, aces conceded and playing faults included.
about.between: Balls that landed untouched within 2.5 m of two teammates about as close as each other. Calling the ball wins them: “Mine!”
about.strengths: What a player brings to the team: what they do better than the others, their presence on the court, their reliability, what they give the others and their points when it counts. Two at most, the rarest in their team first, each from a minimum. Click to replay these moments.
about.toWorkOn: The one thing a player misses most clearly compared with the rest of their team, with at least 5 attempts on each side and a 20-point gap. Click to replay these moments.
about.time: Time on the court during the rallies (minutes:seconds).
about.overReceptions: The receptions that go straight to the other team.
about.overDigs: The digs that go straight to the other team.
about.serveRated: The serves' mean grade, out of 5, from the other team's reception: 5 for an ace or a reception missed, 4 when the reception is poor or sent straight back, 3 when it is good, 2 when it is perfect, 0 for a fault.
about.attackRated: The attacks' mean rating, out of 5, from 5 attacks: 5 winning, 4 no counter-attack, 2 counter-attacked, 1 blocked, 0 another fault.
about.digRated: The digs' mean rating, out of 5, from 5 digs, worked out as for receptions.
about.setsAttacked: The sets followed right after by an attack of their team.
about.setAssists: The winning attacks right after their sets, by a teammate.
about.setFaults: The sets lost: the ball lands, goes out or into the net.

tips.serve: In tight moments, a serve in the court makes the other team build a play.
tips.attack: Look at the block before hitting: a placed ball beats a hit out or blocked.
tips.defense: Get in place before the other team hits, and call who takes the ball.
tips.reception: Share the court before each serve and aim high at the setter.
tips.set: Get under the ball and call who you are setting.
tips.relance: With no attack on, send it high and deep rather than forcing it.
tips.block: Jump straight up, hands above the net, without touching it.
tips.fault: Watch the net, the centre line and the rotation.
